sources.title: Thomas Babcock, Households of the Indigenous K’iche’ Maya at the City of Utatlán (2011)
sources.note: Direct primary research PDF. Printed pages 2 to 4 and 10 to 20; founding and migration reconstructions disputed, so no precise foundation asserted.

sources.title: Micaela Raquel Macario Cálgua, The Inhabitants of Q’umarkaaj (FAMSI, 2006)
sources.note: Direct English translation of the 2004 research report. PDF indices 1, 8, 10, 13, 15 and 17 support topography, household materials, ceramics, obsidian and tentative family expansion.

sources.title: Guatemala Ministry of Culture, Q’umarkaj as an archaeological and sacred place (2026)
sources.note: Direct ministry account, paragraphs on Council of the K’iche’ People and ancestral authorities; Conoce el parque lists plaza, temples and ballcourt.

sources.title: Newberry Library, Popol Vuh research guide
sources.note: Direct manuscript custodian guide. Ximénez manuscript 1700 to 1715; proposed earlier sixteenth-century text distinguished from surviving copy.

sources.title: Allen J. Christenson, Popol Vuh: Literal Translation and Transcription
sources.note: Direct scholarly bilingual edition, first PDF page, third line: WARAL xchiqatz’ib’aj wi / HERE we shall write. Edition prints straight apostrophes; sample preserves them. Modern scholarly transcription of a colonial witness, not a preconquest inscription.

sources.title: Guatemala Ministry of Culture, Maize Day cooking encounter in Quiché (2025)
sources.note: Direct account of 31 August 2025 workshop, 30 students and six teachers, tamalitos de siete camisas locally called Ub’en. No preconquest dating of the recipe inferred.

sources.title: Guatemala Ministry of Culture, K’iche’ language workshop in Nahualá (2026)
sources.note: Direct page extraction incomplete but indexed original fully verifies 21 January workshop for 25 children learning domestic-animal vocabulary. Query: site.noticias.mcd.gob.gt/2026/01/27 K’iche’ niños.

sources.title: Newberry Library, Four Popol Vuh facsimiles distributed across Guatemala (2026)
sources.note: Direct library report, 29 July 2026; four destinations and access for schoolchildren. Does not use the article’s internally inconsistent 115-year custody figure.

sources.title: INPC, Complejo Arqueológico Cerros Hojas-Jaboncillo
sources.note: Original institutional page directly indexed in full: sails, Spondylus, U-shaped stone seats, museum objects and community library. Broad dates vary across INPC pages; not treated as exact origins.

sources.title: INPC, Sitios Arqueológicos Emblemáticos: Hojas-Jaboncillo
sources.note: Original indexed institutional page lists houses, temples, water wells, channels and storage silos; gives broad Manteña chronology 700 to 1520.

sources.title: Jorge Marcos, Recuperación Patrimonial, Proyecto Hojas-Jaboncillo (2011)
sources.note: Direct PDF fetch failed; indexed original text read, sections 1.8 and 2.1 to 2.1.2. Navigation with guaras and hypothesis of hillside surplus production; no ocean crossing or continent-wide uniform empire inferred.

sources.title: Marco Vargas, Análisis espacial del complejo arquitectónico Y (2015)
sources.note: Direct PDF fetch failed; indexed original Introduction read in full. Loma del Secal MIVA2-002 domestic rubbish deposits and eight circular depressions at La Y. Storage function tentative.

sources.title: Pedro Javier Basantes Guañuna, Pesas de red y pesas de buceo procedentes del fondo marino de Salango (2024)
sources.note: Original primary abstract indexed in full; direct fetch failed. Three diving weights, two net weights and anchor found in survey. Multi-period coastal context explicitly retained, not all dated Manteño.

sources.title: Museo de América, Manteño sculptural vessel, inventory 03770
sources.note: Direct fetch failed; complete indexed original museum object page read. Museum warns conventional censer label is incorrect and archaeological contexts poorly documented. Dating 800 to 1532 is a broad object range.

sources.title: Jorge Gómez Rendón, Deslindes lingüísticos en las tierras bajas del Pacífico ecuatoriano, tercera parte (2021)
sources.note: Direct scholarly abstract read. Studies names, ethnohistory and linguistic substrates; migration model explicitly provisional. Does not supply a securely translated preconquest sentence; absence statement is bounded to checked evidence.

sources.title: INPC, Estudios multidisciplinarios en cinco espacios prehispánicos tardíos del Ecuador
sources.note: Indexed original conclusions of study of sixteenth-century Manteño settlements: Charapotó devastated by Alvarado in 1534, reconstituted reduction of four parcialidades; female ruler of Achira; changing colonial place-names. Direct PDF fetch unreliable.

sources.title: INPC, San Biritute: lluvia, amor y fertilidad
sources.note: Original indexed book text read around footnotes 11 to 14: Guancavilca self-identification and collective territory; explicitly distinguishes Guancavilca from broader Manteño-Guancavilca. Direct PDF fetch failed.

sources.title: INPC, Sacachún celebrates the return of San Biritute (2019)
sources.note: Full original indexed text verified removal in 1952 and return on 16 July 2011; 2.35-meter monolith, community campaign and local rain/fertility associations. Direct fetch failed.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Western Guatemalan highlands; plausible approximate placement, not a verified maximum kingdom boundary. One card only; no other Maya people absorbed. Public caveats distinguish map coverage, kingdom and living K’iche’ people.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Christenson literal edition page 1: WARAL xchiqatz’ib’aj wi / HERE we shall write. Straight apostrophes preserved in public sample; 1700 to 1715 surviving manuscript identified separately from older traditions.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Approximate Manabí/Santa Elena coastal polygon. Combined archaeological label, not demonstrated uniform sovereign state; Guancavilca self-identification explicitly distinguished. No distinct modern community or separate indexed culture absorbed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: INPC pages vary between 500 to 1534 and 700 to 1520; first narrative period uses broad contextual 700, not an exact foundation. Imported 1492 to 1500 remains map coverage. Colonial changes occurred after that slice.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: No original sentence claimed. The checked linguistic study works from names and ethnohistory with provisional reconstruction. Decorative motifs are not represented as translated script.
batchIdentityNotes.access: Several INPC and museum pages fail direct fetch but original indexed full passages were verified. Exact queries and locators retained in source notes; no third-party blog assertions used.
